title: AMD Stock Falls 13.2% as Chip Stocks Slide (Nov 20)
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) closed at $424.39 on Nov 20, down 13.25%, as an AI chip sell-off deepened a day after a short report on its China ties.
body_markdown:
## Why AMD Stock Fell


Financial media tied Friday's drop mainly to a sector-wide sell-off. According to[the Associated Press](https://www.nbcconnecticut.com/news/national-international/november-20-stock-market-updates/3798357/) , chip stocks bore the brunt of a sell-off in AI stocks, as worries grew that the sector's big market values and heavy spending are unjustified. The AP added that the selling spread to Asian and European markets and that the PHLX Semiconductor Index fell steeply.


As reported by[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/chips-are-crashing-like-its-2008-as-the-nasdaq-100-nears-a-bear-market-192805534.html) , chip stocks had their worst week since the one after the September 11, 2001 attacks, and the Nasdaq 100 finished just shy of a[bear market](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/bull-market-vs-bear-market-definition-examples-and-how-it-compares/) .


The sector rout came a day after a company-specific blow. Per[TIKR](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/jim-cramer-thank-shortseller-discount-115155790.html) , AMD fell on Thursday, November 19, after Hunterbrook Media published a report titled "AMD Has Its Own China Problem," then kept falling on Friday as tech sold off. Hunterbrook's affiliate, Hunterbrook Capital, is short the stock.


The report said IEIT Systems, a Chinese server maker on a US blacklist, kept loading newer versions of AMD firmware into its server updates, although Hunterbrook said its findings do not establish an export-law violation. AMD said the claims "misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships," TIKR reported.


## AMD Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- According to the company's[third-quarter 2026 results release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000002488/000000248826000188/q32026991.htm) of November 3, revenue grew 45% year over year to a record $13.4 billion, and Data Center segment revenue rose 97% to a record $8.5 billion.
- In the same release, AMD said it expects fourth-quarter revenue of approximately $17 billion, plus or minus 3%, the company's own outlook for its next[earnings report](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/how-to-read-an-earnings-report/) .
- AMD also said Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure are running workloads on its first Helios rack-scale systems.


### Risks


- The Hunterbrook allegations are unresolved: AMD disputes them, and Hunterbrook itself said its findings do not establish an export-law violation, according to TIKR.
- China exposure: TIKR noted that AMD billed 22.4% of its 2025 revenue to China and Hong Kong, and that a Commerce Department rule effective November 19 adds license requirements for advanced US AI chips, AMD's Instinct GPUs included, shipped to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil. TIKR also flagged January 10, when a pause ends on a rule extending blacklist limits to companies at least 50% owned by blacklisted firms.
- Doubts over AI spending: Michael Antonelli of Baird told the AP that the notion that AI can keep spending unlimited amounts of money and support the stock market "is ending as we speak."
